requirements.title: Gate on every route that uses a sandbox
requirements.rationale: A sandbox holds a credential of its creator, so who may act in it, and in which state, must be decided the same way on every route (SBX-FR-010 to SBX-FR-012, §13.3.3).

criteria.condition: a request reaches POST …/exec, PUT …/files, GET …/files, GET …/logs or GET …/attach under /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id on a hub whose configuration has no [sandbox] section
criteria.action: refuse the request after authentication and before the scope and workspace checks
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled, for an existing and for an unknown workspace slug alike; a request without a credential is still HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated

setup: a hub handler under httptest built without a [sandbox] section and with a temporary store, mounting the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go
a user with an API key and one workspace
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the five route-table entries times slug in {existing, unknown}: r = do(method, path, apiKey); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandboxes_disabled'; and one row per entry without a credential: assert r.status == 401 and error_type == 'unauthenticated'

criteria.condition: the caller's PAT lacks sandboxes:read on GET …/files or GET …/logs, or lacks sandboxes:write on POST …/exec, PUT …/files or GET …/attach, or the caller lacks read access to the workspace on a read route or write access on a write route
criteria.action: refuse the request without contacting the runtime
criteria.contract: a PAT without the scope: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, whether or not the workspace exists; a caller who cannot see the workspace: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; a read-only member on exec, PUT …/files or attach: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; the fake runtime records no call

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
the fork's organization has a member M with read-only access to F, and there is a user who is no member
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over (route entry, credential) -> (status, error_type): {each read entry, U's PAT holding sandboxes:write but not sandboxes:read -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each write entry, U's PAT holding only sandboxes:read -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each entry, a PAT without the scope on an unknown slug -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each entry, API key of the non-member -> 404 not_found}; {each write entry, API key of M -> 403 forbidden}; {each read entry, API key of M -> probe reached}: r = do(entry, cred); assert status and error_type; assert the probe was not reached and fakeRuntime.calls == 0 for every refused row

criteria.condition: the :id of the request is unknown, is not of the form sbx_ plus 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or names a sandbox of another workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request as if no such sandbox existed
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type sandbox_not_found on each of the five routes

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
U owns a second workspace with its own sandbox
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the five entries times id in {'sbx_' + 32 zeros, 'nope', the id of the sandbox of U's other workspace}: r = do(entry with id, U's key); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandbox_not_found'; assert the probe was not reached

criteria.condition: a caller with write access calls POST …/exec, PUT …/files or GET …/attach with a credential that does not cover the sandbox's hub credential by the no-widening rule of package 44 (a scope of hub_access.scopes it does not hold, or a paths limit narrower than the sandbox's)
criteria.action: refuse the request before validating its body and before looking at the sandbox's state
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, also when the body is invalid and when the sandbox is stopped; the same credential on GET …/files and GET …/logs is not refused by this rule; the fake runtime records no exec, write or terminal call

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
S's hub_access.scopes holds git:write; PAT W of U holds sandboxes:write and sandboxes:read but not git:write
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the three write entries (exec, put files, attach) times S.state in {ready, stopped} with PAT W: r = do(entry, W); assert r.status == 403 and error_type == 'insufficient_scope' and the probe was not reached; then with PAT W on the two read entries (get files, logs): assert the probe was reached; and with U's API key on the write entries with S ready: assert the probe was reached

criteria.condition: a request passes every earlier check and the sandbox's state is not one the route allows: ready for exec, PUT …/files and attach; ready, completed or failed for GET …/files
criteria.action: refuse the request without contacting the runtime
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type sandbox_not_ready; exec, PUT …/files and attach are refused in provisioning, stopped, completed, failed and deleted; GET …/files is refused in provisioning, stopped and deleted and answered 200 in completed and failed; the fake runtime records no call for a refused request

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over state in {provisioning, ready, stopped, completed, failed, deleted} times the five entries: set S.state in the store; r = do(entry, U's key); refused unless (entry is logs) or (state == ready) or (entry is get files and state in {completed, failed}); for refused rows assert r.status == 409 and error_type == 'sandbox_not_ready' and the probe was not reached; for the other rows assert the probe was reached

criteria.condition: the runtime cannot be reached, or returns a failure, while parleyd serves an exec before its first output, a file transfer before its first byte, or the opening of an attach terminal
criteria.action: answer with the runtime-error answer of package 44, its message being the runtime's text after the scrubbing function of package 45 replaced the sandbox's secret values and cut it to 1,024 bytes
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with error_type sandbox_runtime_error; error.message holds the runtime's text with every secret value of the sandbox replaced by [redacted] and is at most 1,024 bytes; neither the response nor the hub's log holds a secret value; a runtime result of kind unsupported is answered the same way

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go is mounted with the operations of exec, put files, get files and attach replaced by a probe that returns the runtime failure errors.New('boom tok_SECRETVALUE') through the runtime-error answer of package 44
tok_SECRETVALUE is the value of an exposed secret of S, known to the scrubbing function of package 45; the hub's log is captured
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the four entries: r = do(entry, U's key); assert r.status == 502 and error_type == 'sandbox_runtime_error'; assert r.json.error.message contains 'boom' and '[redacted]' and not 'tok_SECRETVALUE'; assert the captured log does not hold 'tok_SECRETVALUE'

criteria.action: for any request to one of the five routes that fails more than one check, answer with the failure of the first check in this order: authentication, sandboxes enabled, binding guard, PAT scope, workspace access, sandbox lookup, no-widening, request validation, sandbox state
criteria.contract: the status and error_type of the earliest failing check in that order

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created

the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
the validation of the exec entry is the real exec body validation or, until it exists, a probe validation that refuses an empty body with 400 invalid_request
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table of POST …/exec requests that each fail two checks -> expected: {PAT without sandboxes:write on a workspace it cannot see -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {the non-member's key with an unknown sandbox id -> 404 not_found}; {U's key, unknown sandbox id, empty body -> 404 sandbox_not_found}; {PAT W of the no-widening test, empty body -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {U's key, empty body, S stopped -> 400 invalid_request}; {a token bound to another workspace and without sandboxes:write -> the binding guard's answer of package 08, not insufficient_scope}: assert status and error_type

requirements.title: Run a command and collect its output
requirements.rationale: An agent drives an idle sandbox with nothing but HTTP: one request, one command, its exit code and output (SBX-FR-030, SBX-FR-032, SBX-US-03).

criteria.condition: an allowed caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/exec with a valid body and no text/event-stream in Accept, for a ready sandbox
criteria.action: run the command through the runtime as the workload user, in the sandbox's working directory or in workdir when given, with the sandbox's environment overlaid by the request's env, with stdin (or the decoded stdin_base64) written to its standard input and then closed, wait for it to end and answer with its result, whether or not the sandbox's main process is running
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {exit_code: int, stdout: string, stderr: string, truncated: false, timed_out: false, duration_ms: int >= 0} and no stdout_base64 or stderr_base64 member; a non-zero exit code is answered 200 with that exit_code

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over (body, fake command behaviour) -> expected: {command ['echo','hi'], prints 'hi\n' exits 0 -> exit_code 0, stdout 'hi\n'}; {exits 3 with stderr 'bad' -> 200, exit_code 3, stderr 'bad'}; {workdir '/tmp', env {A:'1'} -> fake saw dir '/tmp' and env containing A=1 and the sandbox's own variables}; {no workdir -> fake saw the sandbox's working directory}; {env {MODE:'req'} where the sandbox env has MODE=profile -> fake saw MODE=req}; {stdin 'abc' -> fake read 'abc' then EOF}; {stdin_base64 of bytes 00 ff -> fake read those bytes}; {sandbox created with a main command that is still running -> 200}: r = post(exec, body); assert r.status == 200; assert the listed members; assert 'stdout_base64' not in r.json; assert fake ran the command as the workload user

criteria.condition: the exec body has no command, an empty command, a command that is not a list of strings or has more than 256 entries, an env with more than 64 entries or a value over 8192 bytes or a name starting with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_ or a name listed in the sandbox's exposed_secrets, both stdin and stdin_base64, a stdin_base64 that is not base64, a stdin over 4194304 bytes after decoding, or a timeout that is not a duration, is zero or exceeds [sandbox].max_exec_timeout; or the body is larger than 8 MiB
criteria.action: refuse the request and run nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request for each invalid member; HTTP 413 with error_type payload_too_large for a body over 8388608 bytes; the fake runtime records no exec; a command of exactly 256 entries, an env of exactly 64 entries, a stdin of exactly 4194304 bytes and a timeout equal to max_exec_timeout are accepted

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
S's exposed_secrets is ['NPM_TOKEN']
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table of bodies -> status: {} -> 400; {command: []} -> 400; {command: 'ls'} -> 400; {command: 257 entries} -> 400; {command: 256 entries} -> 200; {env: 65 entries} -> 400; {env: 64 entries} -> 200; {env: {A: 8193 bytes}} -> 400; {env: {PARLEY_X: '1'}} -> 400; {env: {OPENSHELL_X: '1'}} -> 400; {env: {NPM_TOKEN: 'x'}} -> 400; {stdin and stdin_base64} -> 400; {stdin_base64: '***'} -> 400; {stdin_base64 of 4194305 bytes} -> 400; {stdin_base64 of 4194304 bytes} -> 200; {timeout: 'soon'} -> 400; {timeout: '0s'} -> 400; {timeout: '31m'} -> 400; {timeout: '30m'} -> 200; {body of 8388609 bytes} -> 413 payload_too_large: r = post(exec, body); assert r.status; for 400 rows assert error_type == 'invalid_request' and fakeRuntime.execs unchanged

criteria.condition: a collected exec's command is still running when its timeout (default 60 s, or the body's timeout) has passed
criteria.action: kill the command through the runtime and answer with the output collected until then
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with timed_out: true, exit_code: null and the stdout and stderr the command wrote before it was killed; the fake runtime records one kill of that command

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
the fake command prints 'partial' and then blocks until killed
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over timeout in {absent -> 60s, '2s' -> 2s}: start post(exec) in a goroutine; wait until fake reports the command running and its output 'partial' written; clock.Advance(limit - 1s); assert no response yet; clock.Advance(1s); r = response; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.timed_out == true and r.json.exit_code == null and r.json.stdout == 'partial'; assert fake.kills == 1

criteria.condition: a collected exec's command writes more than 1048576 bytes to stdout or to stderr
criteria.action: return the first 1048576 bytes of that stream, cut back to the last complete UTF-8 character, drop the rest and keep reading until the command ends
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with truncated: true; the truncated stream's returned bytes are a prefix of what the command wrote and are at most 1048576 bytes; a stream of exactly 1048576 bytes is returned whole with truncated: false; the exit code is the command's

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over (stdout bytes, stderr bytes) -> (truncated, len stdout, len stderr): {1048576 'a', 0} -> (false, 1048576, 0); {1048577 'a', 0} -> (true, 1048576, 0); {10, 2000000 'b'} -> (true, 10, 1048576); {1048575 'a' + 'é' + 'zz', 0} -> (true, 1048575, 0): r = post(exec); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.truncated and lengths; assert r.json.exit_code == the fake's exit code; assert returned stdout is a prefix of the written bytes

criteria.condition: the bytes a collected exec returns for stdout or stderr are not valid UTF-8
criteria.action: return that stream base64-encoded in stdout_base64 or stderr_base64 with its text member empty, and return the other stream as text
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 where, for the non-UTF-8 stream, the text member is "" and the _base64 member decodes to exactly the bytes written (up to the 1 MiB cap); the _base64 member of a valid UTF-8 stream is absent

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes bytes ff fe 00 to stdout and 'ok' to stderr; r = post(exec); assert r.json.stdout == '' and base64decode(r.json.stdout_base64) == bytes ff fe 00; assert r.json.stderr == 'ok' and 'stderr_base64' not in r.json; then swapped streams: assert the mirror image

criteria.condition: the caller's connection closes, or the hub begins to shut down, while a collected exec's command is running
criteria.action: kill the command through the runtime and release its place in the sandbox's exec count
criteria.contract: the fake runtime records one kill of that command within 1 second of the disconnect; a following exec in the same sandbox is accepted; the main process of the sandbox is not killed

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
the fake command blocks until killed; S has a running main process
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: ctx, cancel = context with cancel; start post(exec) with ctx in a goroutine against a real httptest.Server; wait until fake reports the command running; cancel(); eventually(1s) fake.kills == 1; assert fake.mainProcessRunning(S); assert post(exec ['true']).status == 200

criteria.condition: [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs commands started through exec, collected or streamed, are running in the sandbox and another exec request for the same sandbox passes every other check
criteria.action: refuse the new request and start no command
criteria.contract: HTTP 429 with error_type rate_limited and no Retry-After header; the fake runtime records no additional exec; an exec in another sandbox is accepted at the same moment

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs is 2
a second ready sandbox S2 on F
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: start 1 collected and 1 streamed exec in S that block; wait until both run; r = post(exec in S); assert r.status == 429 and error_type == 'rate_limited' and r.header('Retry-After') == ''; assert fake.execs == 2; assert post(exec in S2 ['true']).status == 200; r = post(exec in S with Accept text/event-stream); assert r.status == 429 and Content-Type is application/json

criteria.action: for any exec that has ended, by exit, timeout, kill after a disconnect, or runtime failure, stop counting it toward the sandbox's exec count, and never count the main process or an attach terminal
criteria.contract: after an exec ended in any of those ways, a new exec in the same sandbox is answered as if the ended one had never run; with max_concurrent_execs 1, an exec is accepted while the main process runs and an attach terminal is open

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs is 1
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, with max_concurrent_execs 1 and S running a main process and one open attach: assert post(exec ['true']).status == 200 (main process and attach do not count); then a table over how the first exec ends {exits 0, exits 9, times out, caller disconnects, fake fails mid-command}: run it to its end; assert the next post(exec ['true']).status == 200

requirements.title: Run a command and stream its output
requirements.rationale: A long command's output must arrive while it runs and without a size cap (SBX-FR-031).

criteria.condition: an allowed caller sends a valid POST …/exec whose Accept header names text/event-stream, for a ready sandbox
criteria.action: run the command as for the collected form and send its output as server-sent events while it runs: frames named stdout and stderr in the order the output arrives, each with data {data: string} carrying at most 32768 bytes of output, then exactly one frame named exit, then close the stream
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream and Cache-Control no-cache; the concatenated data of the stdout frames equals the command's stdout and likewise for stderr; the last frame is event exit with data {exit_code: int, timed_out: false, duration_ms: int}; a frame is received before the command ends when the command wrote output and is still running

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 'a' to stdout, waits for a signal, writes 'b' to stderr and 100000 bytes 'c' to stdout, exits 4; open post(exec, Accept: text/event-stream) against httptest.Server; assert status 200 and Content-Type starts with 'text/event-stream'; read first frame == (stdout, {data:'a'}) while fake reports the command running; signal; read to end; assert concat(stdout frames) == 'a' + 100000 'c'; assert concat(stderr frames) == 'b'; assert every frame's decoded data <= 32768 bytes; assert last frame == (exit, {exit_code: 4, timed_out: false}) with duration_ms present; assert the body ends after it

criteria.action: for any amount of output of a streamed exec, deliver every byte of stdout and stderr in frames, with no cap and no truncated member
criteria.contract: the bytes reassembled from the stdout frames equal the bytes the command wrote to stdout, and likewise for stderr, for outputs larger than 1 MiB; no frame carries a truncated member

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 3 MiB of a repeating pattern to stdout and 2 MiB to stderr; read the stream; assert sha256(concat(stdout frames)) == sha256(written stdout) and the same for stderr; assert the exit frame's data has no 'truncated' member

criteria.condition: a chunk of a streamed exec's output is not valid UTF-8
criteria.action: send that chunk in a frame whose data is {data_base64: string} and keep sending valid chunks as {data: string}
criteria.contract: the bytes obtained by decoding data_base64 frames and taking data frames as UTF-8, concatenated in order per stream, equal the bytes the command wrote

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 'ok' then (after a flush) bytes ff 00 fe then 'done' as separate chunks to stdout; read frames; assert the frame for the middle chunk has data_base64 and no data; assert reassembled bytes == 'ok' + ff 00 fe + 'done'

criteria.condition: a streamed exec's command is still running when its timeout has passed
criteria.action: kill the command through the runtime, send the exit frame and close the stream
criteria.contract: the last frame is event exit with data {exit_code: null, timed_out: true, duration_ms: int}; frames for the output written before the kill precede it; the fake runtime records one kill

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 'partial' and blocks; open the stream with timeout '2s'; read frame (stdout, 'partial'); clock.Advance(2s); read last frame; assert it is (exit, {exit_code: null, timed_out: true}); assert fake.kills == 1; assert the body ended

criteria.condition: the caller closes the stream of a streamed exec, or the hub begins to shut down, before the exit frame was sent
criteria.action: kill the command through the runtime and release its place in the sandbox's exec count
criteria.contract: the fake runtime records one kill of that command within 1 second; the main process of the sandbox keeps running

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
S has a running main process
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: open the stream against httptest.Server for a fake command that prints 'x' and blocks; read the first frame; close the response body; eventually(1s) fake.kills == 1; assert fake.mainProcessRunning(S)

criteria.condition: a streamed exec request fails a gate check, the validation of its body or the concurrent exec limit
criteria.action: answer with the same JSON error envelope, status and error_type as the collected form, and open no event stream
criteria.contract: the status and error_type the collected form gives for the same request; Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8; no command is started

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
PAT W as in the no-widening check of internal/sandbox/use_test.go
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table with Accept: text/event-stream over {body without command -> 400 invalid_request}; {timeout '31m' -> 400 invalid_request}; {S stopped -> 409 sandbox_not_ready}; {PAT W without git:write -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {unknown sandbox id -> 404 sandbox_not_found}: r = post(exec); assert r.status and error_type; assert r.header('Content-Type') starts with 'application/json'; assert fake.execs == 0

criteria.condition: the runtime fails after a streamed exec has sent its response headers
criteria.action: end the stream without an exit frame and release the exec's place in the sandbox's count
criteria.contract: the response body ends; the frames received contain no frame named exit; a following exec in the sandbox is accepted

setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs is 1
check.pseudocode: in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go with max_concurrent_execs 1: fake command writes 'x' then the fake fails the exec with an error; read all frames; assert frames == [(stdout, 'x')] and none is named exit; assert post(exec ['true']).status == 200

requirements.title: Upload a file or a tar stream into the working directory
requirements.rationale: An agent puts its inputs into the sandbox without a runtime client, and never outside the working directory (SBX-FR-033).

criteria.condition: an allowed caller sends PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/files with a path inside the working directory, no archive parameter and a body of content type application/octet-stream, for a ready sandbox
criteria.action: write the body through the runtime as the content of the file at path, relative paths resolved against the working directory, creating missing parent directories, replacing an existing file, with the mode given in mode or 0644

criteria.action: send POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/exec with Accept: text/event-stream and without the 30-second request timeout, write the bytes of every stdout frame to stdout and of every stderr frame to stderr as they arrive, and exit with the command's exit code, mapping every value above 125 to 125
criteria.contract: stdout holds exactly the command's stdout bytes and stderr exactly its stderr bytes (data_base64 frames decoded), with nothing added; the exit status is the exit code for 0 to 125 and 125 for a larger one

criteria.action: send workdir, an env member built from the --env values, timeout as given, and with --stdin the whole of its standard input as stdin_base64
criteria.contract: the request body the hub receives is {command, workdir, env: {key: value, ...}, timeout, stdin_base64} with only the members whose flags were given; an --env value containing = after the first one keeps the rest as the value

passes the gate (scope, write access, sandbox found, no widening, state ready), resolves run.sh inside the working directory and writes the file through the runtime client

sends POST …/exec with command ['sh', 'run.sh']
takes an exec slot, runs the command through the runtime client, collects its output and answers 200 with exit_code, stdout and stderr
runs the command as the workload user in the working directory; the script writes result.txt
sends GET …/files?path=result.txt and receives the file's bytes
has set the sandbox's last_activity_at at each operation and has told the operation observers about one upload, one exec and one download
